DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 79 s. 2022 AUG 01 2022 Mr. WARREN LUCENTE 9 Jasmin Dakota St. Casili Hills Subdivision Brgy. Casili, Mandaue City, Province of Cebu warrenlucente@yahoo.com Dear Mr. Lucente: This has reference to your follow-up letter dated II July 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on the following matters, which we quoted in toto: "1. Is there such a thing as a Lupon chairman of the day in the Katarungang Pambarangay Law? Does the chairmanship change from day to day? 2. Whether or not the Lupon Tagapamayapa, in the performance of their duty, should be neutral, unbiased, and objective as mandated by law? 3. Is it proper and ethical for a Lupon Tagapamayapa to influence the filing and hearing of a complaint in the barangay? 4. Whether or not elected barangay councilors are eligible to be a Lupon Tagapamayapa." Per your letter, you filed a criminal case against your neighbor, Mr. James Chicklas, for unjust vexation and grave threats in the trial courts of Mandaue City. Thereafter, your neighbor filed a complaint against you in the barangay. You represented that Sangguniang Barangay (SB) Member Emmanuel Mantilla of Barangay Casili presided as the Lupon Tagapamayapa in the case filed against you in the barangay. You also manifested that Mr. Chicklas managed to obtain the support of SB Member Mantilla in the criminal case, who was the presiding officer in the Katarungang Pambarangay, by being called as Witness of the former in the criminal case. Hence, the instant queries. As to the first query, we submit that there is no such term as "chairman of the day" considering that the chairmanship of the Lupon Tagapamayapa is specifically granted by RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 to the Punong Barangay for a period of three (3) years, thus: "SECTION. 399. Lu on Ta a ama a a.- a There is hereb created in each Baran a a Lu on Ta a ama a a hereinafter referred to as the Iu on com osed of the Punon Baran a as chairman and ten(IC)) to twenty (20) "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

members. The lupon shall be constituted every three (3) years in the manner provided herein." (Emphasis Supplied) xxxx Hence, the incumbent Punong Barangay of Casili shall act as Chairman of the Lupong Tagapamayapa, unless either of the following circumstances is the case in said barangay: 1) When the incumbent Punong Barangay is travelling within the country but outside his/her territorial jurisdiction for a period not exceeding three (3) consecutive days in which case, the Punong Barangay may designate an Officer-in-Charge (OIC) to handle the mediation proceedings, pursuant to Section 46 (c) of the Local Government Code of 1991; or 2) When the incumbent Punong Barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his/her duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad and suspension from office, in which case the highest ranking SB Member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the Punong Barangay, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days; or 3) When the incumbent Punong Barangay is permanently incapacitated to perform his duties for reasons stated under Section 44 of the Local Government Code of 1991. As to the second and third queries, we invite your attention to Rule IV, Section 1 of the Katarungang Pambarangay Rules issued by the Department of Justice, which provides for the qualifications for membership of Lupong Tagapamayapa, thus: "SECTION 1. Qualifications for membership — To qualify for appointment to the Lupon, a person must have his actual residence or place of work in the barangay and must possess personal characteristics that indicate his suitability of conciliation of disputes. Such suitability may be indicated by his inteqriW. impartiality. independence of mind. sense of fairness. reputation for probity. and other relevant consideration such as tact. patience. resourcefulness. flexibility and open-mindedness. Further, he must not be expressly disqualified by law from holding public office." (Emphasis supplied) Clearly and in reply to your queries, the members of the Lupong Tagapamayapa must always be impartial, fair and independent of mind in the performance of their duties. We are of the view that failure to possess such personal characteristics at any given time may be a ground for his ineligibility as a lupon member or from being appointed as such. Also, the primary role of the lupon is to assist the parties in discussing the possible amicable settlement of their disputes. The main strategy for settling disputes is to provide a venue for the disputing parties to search for a solution that is mutually Page 2 of 4

acceptable.l To be able to exercise such critical role, the lupon must constantly be neutral and impartial in administering barangay justice through mediation or conciliation efforts. With respect to the we answer in the negative. While it is true that Section 406 of the LGC and Section 9, Rule IV of the Katarungang Pambarangay Rules states that in the performance of duties, the Lupon members, whether in public or private employment, shall be deemed to be on official time, and shall not suffer from any diminution in compensation or allowance from said employment by reason thereof, the following are disqualified to be Lupon members: 1. Below 18 years of age; 2. Incompetent; 3. Convicted of a crime carrying with it, penalties or perpetual or temporary disqualification from holding public office; 4. Elected Government Official; and 5. Member of Armed Forces who is in the active service.2 Further, Section 94 of the LGC explicitly provides for the prohibition for any elective official to hold any other office or employment during tenure, viz: "Section 94. Appointment of Elective and Appointive Local Officials; Candidates Who Lostin an Election. - (a) No elective or appointive local official shall be eliqible for appointment or desiqnation in any capacity to any public office or position durinq his tenure. Unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position no elective or appointive local official shall hold any other office or employment in the qovernment or any subdivision. agency or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries." (Emphasis and underlining ours) Accordingly, the appointment of the sanggunian barangay member as a member of the lupon tagapamayapa is a violation of the prohibition on appointment of elective local officials. Along this line, may we respectfully correct the term "barangay councilors" that you used in your fourth query. Under the Local Government Code of 1991, there is no such term as "barangay councilor". The regular members of the sangguniang barangay which we often refer to as "barangay councilors" or "barangay kagawads" are aptly called "sangguniang barangay members" under the Local Government Code of 1991. 1 Katarungang Pambarangay, A Handbook, 2004, Philippines-Canada Local Govemment Support Program (LGSP) .http:llregion5.dilg.gov.ph]attachments/articl ell barangay_Hand book 2 Page II, Katarungang Pambarangay, A Handbook, 2004, Philippines-Canada Local Government Support (LGSP).http•]/region5.dilg.gov.ph/attachments/articte/182/ReIated_Laws_Katarungang_Pambarangay_Handbook .pdf Page 3 of 4

The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same, and shall be without prejudice to the contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Undersec tary for Local Government OUSLG/MLl/LLLS/LRALLD/lasm/clp copy furnished: DIR. LEOCADIO T.
